overview.description: Dou Dizhu (Fight the Landlord) is a Chinese climbing game for three players. One player becomes the landlord by winning an auction (bid 1, 2 or 3) and plays alone against the other two in partnership. Players shed cards by playing singles or valid combinations; the landlord leads and each player in turn must pass or beat the previous play. Rocket (two jokers) and bomb (four of a kind) are special combinations. The first side to empty their hand wins the hand; payment is the bid amount times multipliers for bombs and rockets.
overview.deck: Standard 52-card pack plus two jokers (red and black), 54 cards total.

history.origins: Dou Dizhu is said to have originated in Hubei province. The name (literally 'fighting the landlord') reflects the class struggle during China's land reform of the 1950s, when peasants were encouraged to oppose landlords. The game has become very popular across China in the last twenty years and is widely played online; the name no longer carries negative connotation.
timeline: Originated in Hubei province; popular across China; became very popular in the last 20 years.

setup.players: Three players; four-player variant uses a double deck.
setup.deck: 54-card pack: standard 52 cards plus two jokers (red and black). Suits are irrelevant; rank from high to low is red joker, black joker, 2, A, K, Q, J, 10 down to 3.
setup.equipment: Standard 52-card deck plus two jokers (red and black).
setup.dealing: One player shuffles and gives the deck to the player to his left to cut. Cards are stacked face down in the centre. One card is turned face up and inserted near the middle to determine who starts the auction. Players then draw from the top counter-clockwise: each looks at their card without showing. Drawing continues until each player has 17 cards. The last three cards remain face down until after the auction; the winning bidder (landlord) adds them to their hand for 20 cards total.

rules.objective: The landlord aims to be the first to play out all their cards in valid combinations. The opposing team wins if either of them empties their hand before the landlord.
rules.gameplay: After the deal, an auction (bids 1, 2 or 3) determines the landlord; the player who drew the face-up card bids first. The highest bidder takes the three face-down cards (20 total) and leads. Each player in turn must pass or beat the previous play with a higher combination of the same type and same number of cards. Rocket (two jokers) beats anything; a bomb (four of a kind) beats any non-rocket combination. When two consecutive players pass, the cards are put aside and the last player to play leads any card or combination. Play continues until one side has no cards left.
keyRules: Thirteen combination types: single, pair, triplet, triplet with single, triplet with pair, sequence (5+), sequence of pairs (3+), sequence of triplets (2+), sequence of triplets with attached cards, sequence of triplets with attached pairs, bomb (four of a kind), rocket (two jokers), quadplex set (quad plus two singles or two pairs).
Rocket beats everything; bomb beats everything except rocket or a higher bomb.

Landlord runs out first: each opponent pays the landlord the bid (1, 2 or 3 units); each bomb or rocket played doubles the payment. Opponent runs out first: landlord pays the bid to each opponent, again doubled per bomb or rocket.
Spring bonus: if opponents play no cards, payment to landlord is doubled; if landlord plays only their first lead and opponents win, landlord payment to opponents is doubled.

validPlays.notes: Beat the previous play with the same combination type and higher rank; 3 low to red joker high. Rocket (two jokers) and bomb (four of a kind) have special override rules.

When leading or after two consecutive passes, play any legal combination: single, pair, triplet, triplet with single or pair, sequence (5+), sequence of pairs (3+), sequence of triplets (2+), bomb, rocket, quadplex set.
Rocket beats everything; bomb beats any non-rocket combination; higher bomb beats lower bomb.
